### Definition of `palloc`

PostgreSQL's `palloc()` function performs dynamic memory allocation inside Postgres itself rather than relying directly on standard library malloc/free APIs. It provides fine-grained control over lifecycle management making custom pooling possible alongside automatic cleanup through contexts tied closely to transaction boundaries. Usage patterns help minimize fragmentation while enforcing strict limits preventing excessive consumption beyond configured values (`work_mem`, `shared_buffers`, etc.).

By leveraging internal allocators, Postgres ensures predictability regarding both space utilization and runtime behavior avoiding external interference caused by global heaps often associated with general-purpose allocators.
